hero.headline: Your data has a home now.
hero.sub: One lakehouse with dashboards built in. Bring every source in, keep it in open tables, and ask for answers in plain language.

sources.headline: Everything flows in.
sources.sub: Databases, files, streams, APIs and business apps land in one place, on a schedule or as they change.
sources.caption: Live change capture for PostgreSQL. Dedupe or keep history on load, discover tables in any source, and upload 10 files at once, in folders.

bronze.title: As it came.
bronze.body: Kept as sent, in open Apache Iceberg tables.

silver.title: Cleaned and checked.
silver.body: Pipelines fix it. Quality checks flag the rest.

gold.title: Ready for answers.
gold.body: Refreshes itself within the lag you set.

sr.bronze: Five example order rows from an orders file and a CRM export, stored as they came. One order arrives twice, Jakarta is spelt three ways, the dates use three formats and one amount is missing.
sr.silver: The same rows in one Silver table. The duplicate is gone, every city reads Jakarta or Bandung, every date has one format, and a quality check flags the one empty amount.
sr.gold: A Gold table of revenue by city built from those rows, Jakarta first, then Bandung, within its target lag, ready for dashboards and the assistant.

assistant.headline: Ask, don't dig.
assistant.sub: Ask in plain words. Anything risky waits for a person.
assistant.name: Assistant
assistant.userOne: Which region had the most visitors last quarter?
assistant.answerOne: Region North had the most visitors last quarter.
assistant.srDescription: An illustration of the assistant. A person asks which region had the most visitors last quarter; the assistant reads a Gold table, groups it by region and answers with a bar chart where North leads. The person then asks to pause the nightly sales pipeline. The assistant does not do it on its own: it shows a request that waits for approval, and an admin approves it. The region names and numbers are illustrative.

dashboards.headline: Answers come back up as dashboards.
dashboards.sub: About two dozen chart types, maps on your own boundaries included.
features: Public links with expiry and password

governance.headline: Guarded by default.
governance.sub: Roles decide who sees what, down to the column.
governance.tableCaption: Five fictional customers. As an analyst the name and email columns are masked; as an admin they are shown in full.

status.analyst: Showing as Analyst: names and emails masked
status.admin: Showing as Admin: every column in full

governance.piiTip: Personal data, masked for roles without access

proof.title: Masking, tested
proof.line: An automated acceptance test checks it end to end.

audit.title: Every action, logged
audit.line: Risky assistant actions wait for a person.

code.sr: A few lines of the Lakehouse's own source code: the function that holds a risky assistant action for a person to approve, and refuses it when there is nowhere to keep the approval.

hosting.label: Where it runs

console.label: The console's home, recreated
console.caption: Ask in plain words, or start from a shortcut.
console.alt: The RantAI Lakehouse console's home, recreated: a box to ask the assistant, with Ask, Build and Tools, and three shortcuts: Connect a source, Create a pipeline and Build a dashboard.

getStarted.headline: Up and running in three steps.

steps.title: Clone it
steps.note: The public repository, with everything the stack needs.

steps.title: Configure it
steps.note: This writes `.env` with generated secrets. Then set `AUTH_BOOTSTRAP_EMAIL` and `AUTH_BOOTSTRAP_PASSWORD` in it: that is your first account.

steps.title: Start it
steps.note: Then open `http://localhost:3000` and sign in with that account.

final.headline: Come on in. The data's fine.
